seoFaq.q1: How do I convert a PDF to Excel?
seoFaq.a1: Upload your PDF to the converter and click Convert. Our AI detects every table in the document — row and column boundaries, merged cells, and headers — and rebuilds it as a native Excel workbook (.xlsx). Once the PDF to Excel conversion finishes, download the file and open it in Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, or LibreOffice Calc. Everything stays editable: numbers as numbers, dates as dates, and text as text. If your PDF has tables scattered across several pages, we merge them into one continuous spreadsheet so you get all your data in a single sheet.
seoFaq.q2: How do I extract a table from a PDF into Excel?
seoFaq.a2: You do not need to copy, screenshot, or retype anything. Just upload the PDF and our table extraction engine maps the grid structure — rows, columns, headers, and merged cells — and exports each table as an Excel range. Tables that continue across pages are detected and joined into one continuous sheet, and you can limit the extraction to specific pages (for example 1,3-7) before converting. The extracted cells stay fully editable, so you can sort, filter, and recalculate the data after the PDF to Excel conversion.
seoFaq.q3: Is the PDF to Excel converter free to use?
seoFaq.a3: Yes. Every new user receives free starter credits, and each PDF to Excel conversion costs only a small number of credits per page. That means you can convert a PDF to Excel for free right away — no subscription, no credit card, and no software to install. If you need to convert many documents, you can purchase additional credits and pay only for what you convert. There is no watermark and no limit on how many tables a single PDF can contain.
seoFaq.q4: Can I convert a scanned PDF to an editable Excel spreadsheet?
seoFaq.a4: Yes. The PDF to Excel converter includes AI OCR, so scanned statements, photographed tables, and image-based PDFs work just like digital ones. The OCR reads the text from the page, then the table extraction engine reconstructs rows, columns, and headers from the recognized content. Bank statements, handwritten inventory sheets, and old scanned reports all convert into spreadsheets you can actually edit and analyze.
seoFaq.q5: Can I also save an Excel file as a PDF or import a PDF into Excel directly?
seoFaq.a5: Microsoft Excel itself can import a PDF using Data → From PDF, which is handy for a quick conversion. But that built-in import often scrambles complex layouts and fails on scanned files. For reliable results, use our PDF to Excel converter and open the resulting .xlsx in Excel. And if you need the opposite direction — exporting an Excel sheet as a PDF — open the file in Excel or Google Sheets and use Save As / Download as PDF; your spreadsheet will be captured with its current layout, ready to share or print.
